text:
alex: FYI I noticed a perf regression in canary after the new kernel-selection change — tail latency spikes on small prompt traffic when microbatching is enabled
maya: saw it too. appears correlated to the classifier picking the 'fast-decode' kernel for ~<64-token prompts, then batches stall waiting for larger decode-rate peers
tom: do we have profiler traces? could be KV prefetch interplay (priming not happening for thin requests)
sasha: throwing the flametrace: ```
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] decode_wait  18ms
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] batch_assemble  40ms
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] kv_prefetch    95ms
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] kernel_launch  6ms
```
alex: kv_prefetch is high on those latencies — but only when batch size < 4. When batch hits >=4, prefetch amortizes. Means microbatch admission policy is letting singles through instead of holding a 20ms window
maya: classifier is mapping by prompt_length bucket and decode_rate bucket. Looks like some samples end up in 'mid-decode' bucket that we recently merged. That merge probably widened admission thresholds
tom: hypothesis: kernel selection combined with widened decode-rate bucket causes imbalance: fast-decode kernel selects smaller per-request budget -> queue policy doesn't hold long enough to accumulate amortized KV prefetch
alex: agree. Quick mitigation: increase token_budget_target for the fast-decode kernel from 32 -> 48 for next canary so admission holds an extra turn. Also set a conservative queue_delay_ms=25 for microbatch pool
sasha: can we simulate? I ran a short sim with synthetic workload (70% 20-40 token prompts, 30% >200 tokens). With token_budget_target=48 latency p95 improved 18% and cost +1.2%
maya: nice. We should also consider splitting the mid-decode bucket into two: mid-slow and mid-fast (decode_rate threshold at 0.8x current). That reduces misclassification of tails
tom: add a telemetry flag to capture classifier->kernel decisions with these fields: prompt_len_bucket, decode_rate_bucket, chosen_kernel, batch_size_at_launch, kv_prefetch_ms. We'll need about 50k samples to be confident
alex: agreed. plan: 1) push canary with token_budget_target bump + queue_delay override (canary id rmicro-2026-03-18-a) 2) enable telemetry flag (off by default) 3) run 6h smoke and gather 50k samples 4) if p95 improved and no cost regressions >3%, promote
sasha: test note: also watch for KV eviction churn in <32 token flows — we saw slight increase in evictions in the sim. Might need to tune kv_hold_ms per pool
maya: adding that to runbook. Also we'll gate the bucket split behind an AB test to verify throughput/cost tradeoffs
infra-bot: deploy request queued: rmicro-2026-03-18-a -> canary nodes (3) scheduled in us-west-2
tom: I'll own telemetry ingestion and dashboard slices. alex will run the canary checks. ping me if you want realtime traces
alex: thanks all. I'll kick off the deploy in 5 and post quick results here. :thumbsup:
